heading: Licensing & Codes
body: No person may drive a motor vehicle on a public road except under a licence issued in terms of the National Road Traffic Act, and must keep that licence (or document) with them in the vehicle.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: A licence to drive a motor vehicle is issued by a driving licence testing centre, and is either a provisional licence (a learner's licence) or a full driving licence.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: A learner's licence application is made at a DLTC on form LL1, accompanied by two identical photos, acceptable identification (plus a copy), and the appropriate fee; applicants 65 or older must also submit a medical certificate (form MC) from a medical practitioner or occupational health practitioner.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: A licence holder who permanently changes their place of residence must notify the registering authority of their new residential and postal address within 14 days.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: An owner, operator, or person in charge of a vehicle may not employ or permit anyone to drive it on a public road unless that person is licensed to drive it.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: A person may not drive a motor vehicle of a prescribed class without a professional driving permit (kept with them in the vehicle), except a learner accompanied by someone registered as a professional driver for that class.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: A motor vehicle licence and licence disc are valid for 12 months from the first day of the month of issue; the expiry date is shown on both.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: The owner of a vehicle is responsible for all offences committed with it on a public road, if the owner permitted its use.

heading: Licensing & Codes
body: A motor vehicle may still be operated for up to 21 days after its licence expires (a 'period of grace'), provided the previous licence number and disc are displayed in the prescribed manner.

heading: Definitions
body: To 'cross' a public road means to move in a direction that intersects the normal course of travel of traffic on that road.

heading: Definitions
body: 'Drawing' means towing a vehicle that is designed or adapted solely to be drawn, using a vehicle designed or adapted solely for that purpose -- as distinct from general 'towing'.

heading: Definitions
body: A driving licence card is a driving licence card issued in terms of the National Road Traffic Act.

heading: Definitions
body: 'Driving time' is any period a driver occupies the driver's seat of a vehicle while it is being operated on a public road, or while the engine is running.

heading: Definitions
body: An emergency brake is a brake, other than the service brake, that is able to stop a vehicle.

heading: Definitions
body: The 'front end' of a vehicle is the part that projects furthest forward (for a semi-trailer, a line through the kingpin connecting the vehicle's widest point ahead of it).

heading: Definitions
body: An instructor is someone who, for direct reward, teaches another person to drive a motor vehicle, or teaches the rules of the road or road signs for a learner's or driving licence.

heading: Definitions
body: The kerb line is the boundary between the shoulder and the verge, or, where there's no shoulder, the boundary between the edge of the roadway and the verge.

heading: Definitions
body: A medical practitioner is a person registered as such under the Medical, Dental and Supplementary Health Service Professions Act.

heading: Definitions
body: To 'operate on a public road' means to use or drive a vehicle (or permit it to be used or driven), or to have or permit a vehicle to be on a public road.

heading: Definitions
body: Overall length is the distance between the front end and rear end of a vehicle, or (for a combination) between the front of the leading vehicle and the rear of the rearmost vehicle.

heading: Definitions
body: Overall height is the distance from ground level to the highest point of the vehicle or its load, excluding overhead electrical contacting gear or a catwalk on electrically driven vehicles.

heading: Definitions
body: Overall width is the distance between two planes parallel to the vehicle's centre-line, touching the widest projecting points on either side -- excluding side mirrors, direction indicators, or small fitments like air deflectors.

heading: Definitions
body: The 'owner' of a vehicle is the person with the right to use and enjoy it under common law or a contractual agreement, or a motor dealer in possession of it for sale.

heading: Definitions
body: To 'park' means to keep a vehicle stationary for longer than is reasonably necessary to load or unload people or goods, excluding delays beyond the driver's control.

heading: Definitions
body: A parking brake is a brake, normally a hand brake, used to keep a vehicle stationary.

heading: Definitions
body: The 'rear end' of a vehicle is the part that projects furthest to the rear.

heading: Definitions
body: 'Roadworthy', for a vehicle, means it complies with the relevant legal provisions and is otherwise fit to be operated on a public road.

heading: Definitions
body: A service brake is a brake, normally a footbrake, used to reduce a vehicle's speed or bring it to a stop.

heading: Definitions
body: A sidewalk is the portion of a verge intended for the exclusive use of pedestrians.

heading: Definitions
body: To 'stop' means to bring a vehicle to a standstill.

heading: Definitions
body: 'The Act' refers to the National Road Traffic Act, 1996 (Act No. 93 of 1996), which governs road traffic in South Africa.

heading: Definitions
body: 'Towing' means towing a vehicle that is not designed or adapted solely to be drawn -- as distinct from 'drawing', which refers to vehicles built solely for that purpose.
